title: Admin: Mike and Jim only (Cloudflare Access)
body:
Locks `/admin/` and its numbers to Mike and Jim.

- **The page:** Cloudflare Access puts a login in front of `gardeninsound.website/admin/`. You type your email, and if it's on the list Cloudflare emails a one-time code. This part is set up in the dashboard, not in code (relay/README.md, "Admin access").
- **The numbers:** the relay no longer serves the public `/stats` and `/traffic`. The admin page reads them from `gardeninsound.website/admin/api/…`, a route of the relay on the site's own zone, so the same login covers them. The relay also checks each request's signed Access token itself (`relay/src/access.ts`: signed by the team's key, for this application, not expired), so the numbers stay locked even if the Access policy were loosened by mistake. Until `ACCESS_TEAM` and `ACCESS_AUD` are set, it answers "locked".
- The game's count pings (`POST /count`) work as before.

**Checked:**
- Unit tests sign real tokens with a test key: a good one gets in; a wrong application, wrong team, expired token, unknown key or someone else's key does not.
- A test fails if `ACCESS_DEV` (the local-only bypass) ever appears in `wrangler.jsonc`.
- `relay/npm test`: the numbers work with the local bypass. Without it, they're locked, a made-up token is refused, and the old public addresses return 404.
- The smoke test still runs the admin page on made-up data.

## Story

Idea: Restrict the admin page to Mike and Jim.
Where: none
Tags: behind-the-scenes
Asked vs made: As asked. The data behind the page is locked too, not just the page, and the relay checks the login itself as a second lock.
Mike:
Note: Needs the Access application set up in the Cloudflare dashboard; then ACCESS_TEAM and ACCESS_AUD go in wrangler.jsonc.
